name: Interdisciplinary Lecture Series Environment: Politics and Society
description:
What does it mean to live on a planet that is quite literally burning — and what does it mean when we are the ones fuelling the flames? Why do wildfires and heatwaves keep breaking records year after year, and what do they reveal about the energy systems we've built to power our lives? Who is most exposed to extreme heat and burning landscapes, and what would it take to move beyond the fuels driving this crisis?
Fire and heat connect to a set of urgent, interlocking problems. Understanding these challenges also means recognizing fire as a natural force that shapes ecosystems and societies, from wildfires and peatland fires to controlled burning and traditional fire management. But the conditions under which fire occurs are changing. Human-driven climate change is altering where, when, and how intensely fires burn, while heatwaves, marine heatwaves, and rising urban temperatures increasingly affect people,
agriculture, and ecosystems. At the same time, human activities are changing the balance and adding fuel to a warming world: burning fossil fuels, extracting resources, heating buildings, transporting people, producing and discarding goods, and transforming landscapes. These connections raise broader questions about energy, consumption, justice, land use, and how humans can learn to live with fire in a changing climate.
The lecture series "Burn, Baby, Burn: Fueling the Climate Crisis" invites you to explore these connections through diverse perspectives and expertise. Each week, speakers from science, industry, policy, and civil society will share insights into the flames we can see and the systems that feed them. Throughout the series, interactive discussions will create space to reflect on energy transitions, resilience, and accountability, and to ask what it takes to cool down a planet that keeps heating up.

---------------------------------------------------

The Environmental Lecture Series is an interdisciplinary, public series of lectures by the Environmental Department of the Student Representation of the Technical University of Munich. It is organized by students of the TU Munich on a voluntary basis.

Since 1985, speakers have been giving lectures on e.g. technical environmental protection, health, consumer and climate protection. It offers both students and teachers at the TUM, as well as the non-university public, the opportunity to get information about current ecological topics and research results at a scientific level. The speakers from research, associations, authorities, nature conservation organizations and companies will be pleased to answer questions from the audience after the lecture.
